completenessChecks: 19 narrative and answer paragraphs, 14 bold interviewer prompts, 1 bold third-person lead-in (the Trump sentence, kept bold as printed and not counted as a prompt) and 3 section headings, in the Hebrew order.

The one body hyperlink (Poli House hotel) kept on the same words with the original atmag URL.
The printed byline and 'Published' line are dropped from the body, as in the W003 and W186 references; the byline as printed is recorded above.
No '—' anywhere; no added sentences, explanations or closing line.
voiceChecks: Opening 'On paper... In practice...' kept, with the Rahamim / Regev comparison and the 'God is not in the details but in the general vibe' twist landing at the end of its sentence.

The 'Rashid-land' paragraph keeps its accumulation (sofas, bathrooms, water bottles, tape dispensers; Pepsi, wastebasket, manhole covers, sneakers) and its two parentheticals; the lateness joke keeps its concession ('and still, when he finally arrives...').

The narrator's pivot to criticizing Rashid's own cheapness ('Since we're talking about other people, it may be time to pause for a little criticism closer to home') keeps the mock-formal setup and the Dizengoff Center gift-shop verdict; the Ra'anana aunt stays.
Rashid's speech is spoken English, not back-translated prose: 'don't ask me', 'boom boom boom, done', 'analog bullshit', 'Disney's rules... are bullshit'. Nothing sanitized.
Ending kept on his line: 'I want to break the conventions, and I do it in pink.'

decisions: Headline 'האוטופיה של קארים ראשיד' kept as 'Karim Rashid's Utopia'; it is a clean headline in both languages.
Subtitle: 'עתיד ורוד לעיצוב' rendered 'design's rosy future' so the pink pun survives as 'rosy'.
'מעצב אווירה' rendered 'a designer of atmosphere', with 'something else entirely:' added as the English carrier for בכלל.
'הפאסון' (White House answer) rendered 'the posturing'; 'בטן מלאה' rendered 'plenty to get off his chest'; 'הוא מרים' rendered 'he crows'.
'שארם ולוק הורס' rendered 'charm and a killer look'; 'לכבוש בקלילות' rendered 'win a room without trying'.
The publisher typo 'הייתי מעצב לו' (first person) is rendered as the intended second-person prompt 'Would you design one of his houses?'; the Hebrew is untouched.
The Bioneers coinage kept as Rashid states it: 'a cross between Pioneers and Binary'.
'Offect Orgy' kept as the publisher spells the brand (the maker spells it Offecct); 'the Poli House' spelled as the hotel spells it.
'מישל גבניט' kept as 'Michel Gavnit' pending verification.
lostInTranslation: The Hebrew's own transliterated English ('וייב', 'קז'ואל', 'צ'יפיות', 'לוק', 'ריפרש') simply becomes English; the code-switch texture is gone and was not compensated.
'זיל הזול' is a set Hebrew phrase with a slightly archaic ring; 'Dirt Cheap' is plainer.
defectsFixed: 'Rashid seems to have carefully produced the experience of meeting him' and 'this is a kingdom that is entirely Rashid-land' rebuilt as English sentences with the verdict last.
'a matter of some tens of millions of dollars' (calque) became 'runs to some tens of millions of dollars'.
'who knows how to conquer effortlessly with charm and a killer look' became 'who knows how to win a room without trying, on charm and a killer look'.
'the nails painted with polish' became 'the lacquered fingernails'; 'pulls out existential insights at a dizzying pace' became 'fires off existential insights at a dizzying clip'.

'Speaking of others, there's room to pause for a moment for a little self-criticism' (which read as the narrator criticizing himself) became 'Since we're talking about other people, it may be time to pause for a little criticism closer to home'.
'raises every so often a slight feeling of cheapness' became 'does occasionally give off a faint whiff of cheapness'.
'the Soho gift shop in Dizengoff Center for the aunt from Ra'anana' now tells an English reader what Soho is and where Dizengoff Center is.

Quotes de-calqued throughout: 'The pictures don't do the place justice' became 'The photos don't do the place any favors'; 'It's so clear to me what's going to be' became 'It's so clear to me what's coming'; 'Cheap materials and accessible technology represent today for me' became '...to me, are what today looks like'; 'Here too he has a bellyful' became 'He has plenty to get off his chest here too'.
The byline aside '(byline as printed: "By New York, Nimrod Dvir")' removed from the translation note line and kept in this record.
Captions moved directly under their provenance comments (no blank line), matching the reference files.
